repos.studentId_extraction_approach: Two-stage Location-header + HTML-script extraction; both rely on the jxglstu.eams5 backend using 302 redirects to embed the studentId in the URL, and the rendered course-table page embedding bizTypeId inside an inline <script> tag

stage1_parseStudentId_from_redirect_head.rationale: GET /eams5-student/for-std/course-table responds 302 with Location header pointing to /for-std/course-table/info/<studentId>; substringAfter trims the path prefix and .toInt() converts. Also handles session-expiry detection (Location contains '/login').

stage2_parseBizTypeId_from_html_script.rationale: After studentId is known, fetch /for-std/course-table/info/<studentId>. The rendered HTML contains an inline <script> with `bizTypeId: <id>` (plus semesterId and dataId). Jsoup selects all script tags and runs a regex `bizTypeId\s*:\s*(\d+)` to extract the integer.

notes: Two distinct extraction sources: redirect header for studentId, HTML <script> regex for bizTypeId
Requires OkHttp .followRedirects(false) (set in JxglstuServiceCreator) so the 302 isn't followed silently and the Location header remains accessible
Supports webVPN fallback (Constant.JXGLSTU_WEBVPN_URL) for off-campus use

repos.studentId_extraction_approach: Single-step Location-header extraction: followRedirects(false) on a GET to STUDENT_INFO_URL (= http://jxglstu.hfut.edu.cn/eams5-student/for-std/student-info) which 302-redirects to /for-std/student-info/info/<studentId>; split Location header on '/' and take index 5

parseStudentId_from_redirect.rationale: GET /eams5-student/for-std/student-info → 302 → /for-std/student-info/info/<studentId>. Splits the Location URL by '/' and takes index 5. Whether this works depends entirely on whether the Location header is absolute (http://...) or relative (/eams5-student/...).

split_analysis.verdict: Code works only if the server returns a relative-path Location header. If it returns absolute (most modern servers do for 302s), split('/')[5] returns 'student-info' (not a number), which would silently propagate as a bogus stuId and explode later when used as the dataId query parameter.

parseStudentId_from_redirect.bug_or_unknown: CONFIRMED BUG for absolute-URL redirects. The fix would be either .substringAfterLast('/') (cleanest, always correct) or .split('/').last (safer than fixed index).

notes: POTENTIAL BUG: response.header('Location').split('/')[5] returns 'student-info' for absolute-URL redirects, not the studentId

Student.login() does call getStuId() so the bug WOULD bite if executed against current jxglstu (which returns absolute URLs) — Student.login() would store the wrong stuId in Credential, and downstream CourseCrawler would 400/500 on dataId='student-info'

All subsequent CourseCrawler code uses the stuId from Credential (not from a fresh extraction) and passes it as dataId form param to /course-table/get-data and as JSON studentId field to /ws/schedule-table/datum
Hard-coded SEMESTER_BACHELOR_ID='2' (undergrad bizTypeId) — different from Chiu-xaH's discover-via-regex approach

cross_verification_findings.topic: 302 Location header is the canonical studentId source
cross_verification_findings.evidence: Both Chiu-xaH (active, 2024+) and BoynChan (2019) extract studentId from the 302 Location header returned by /for-std/course-table (Chiu) or /for-std/student-info (Boyn). They pick slightly different endpoints but use the same mechanism: turn off follow-redirects, read Location, parse the trailing path segment.

cross_verification_findings.topic: BoynChan split-index bug for absolute-URL Location headers
cross_verification_findings.evidence: BoynChan StudentInfoCrawler.getStuId uses response.header('Location').split('/')[5]. For an absolute URL like 'http://jxglstu.hfut.edu.cn/eams5-student/for-std/student-info/info/123456', split('/')[5] = 'student-info' (not the studentId, which is at [7]). Only works if the server returns a relative-path Location header.
cross_verification_findings.fix_suggestion: Use .substringAfterLast('/') or .split('/').last() — both always return the last path segment regardless of absolute vs relative URL form.

cross_verification_findings.topic: bizTypeId is discovered from page HTML, not hard-coded
cross_verification_findings.evidence: Chiu-xaH's parseBizTypeId regex `bizTypeId\s*:\s*(\d+)` runs against the rendered HTML's <script> tags. This is more robust than BoynChan's hard-coded SEMESTER_BACHELOR_ID='2' — different bizTypeId values exist for undergrad (2), grad (3?), continuing-ed, exchange, etc.

cross_verification_findings.topic: Two-step call sequence is universal across both EAMS5 implementations
cross_verification_findings.evidence: Chiu-xaH and BoynChan both use: (1) get-data (GET with bizTypeId+semesterId+dataId) to obtain lessons[] + lessonIds[], then (2) schedule-table/datum (POST with studentId+lessonIds+weekIndex) to obtain scheduleList + lessonList. This is the canonical EAMS5 schedule fetch protocol.

cross_verification_findings.topic: Aoi-cn provides no extraction code (closed-source backend)
cross_verification_findings.evidence: All schedule/login calls go to private cloud endpoints (/login, /schedule, /exam_arrange, /select_info). The repo is a frontend only.

cross_verification_findings.topic: elonzh/django-hfut-auth targets legacy system, not EAMS5
cross_verification_findings.evidence: requirements.txt pins hfut>=1.4.1. The hfut package on PyPI (v1.4.1, downloaded and inspected) targets http://ids1.hfut.edu.cn/amserver/UI/Login (CAS portal for legacy jw.hfut.edu.cn). Zero references to jxglstu.hfut.edu.cn or eams5-student anywhere in the upstream package.

recommended_reference_for_modern_impleme: Chiu-xaH/HFUT-Schedule (149 stars, active Kotlin/Android codebase) — particularly JxglstuRepository.kt parseStudentId (Location header substringAfter) and parseBizTypeId (Jsoup script-tag regex). The 2024-era code is the most authoritative public reference for the current EAMS5 contract.
